1.title: Routing Technologies and NAT
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Routing Technologies and nat. It covers the exam area two point zero Network Implementation. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. two point one Explain characteristics of routing technologies: static and dynamic routing (B G P, E I G R P, O S P F). Route selection (administrative distance, prefix length, metric). Address translation (nat, P A T). First hop redundancy protocol (F H R P). Virtual I P (V I P). Subinterfaces. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two point zero Network Implementation (twenty percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Static and dynamic routing
1.text: Static and dynamic routing. Static routing. An administrator enters each route manually; simple, predictable, no overhead; does not adapt to failures. Dynamic routing. Routers exchange routes with a protocol and adapt to changes. O S P F (Open Shortest Path First). Type: Link-state, interior. Notes: Open standard, areas, metric equals cost. E I G R P (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol). Type: Advanced distance-vector, interior. Notes: Cisco-origin, metric from bandwidth and delay. B G P (Border Gateway Protocol). Type: Path-vector, exterior. Notes: Routes between autonomous systems (the internet).

1.title: Route selection
1.text: Route selection. When several routes match a destination, the router chooses in this order.

1.title: Route selection, continued
1.text: Route selection. The figure shows this: Route selection: longest prefix first, then lowest administrative distance, then lowest metric.

1.title: Route selection, continued
1.text: Route selection. one. Prefix length. The most specific (longest) prefix wins, for example slash twenty-six beats slash twenty-four. two. Administrative distance (A D). Lower A D equals more trusted source. three. Metric. Lower metric within the same protocol. Typical administrative distances: connected zero, static one, e B G P twenty, E I G R P ninety, O S P F one hundred ten, R I P one hundred twenty. Exam tip: Longest prefix first, then administrative distance, then metric. A default route (zero dot zero dot zero dot zero slash zero) is used only when nothing more specific matches.

1.title: Address translation
1.text: Address translation. nat (network address translation). Translates private to public addresses; static nat one-to-one, dynamic nat from a pool. P A T (port address translation, also nat overload). Many private hosts share one public I P, distinguished by port numbers.

1.title: Redundancy and interfaces
1.text: Redundancy and interfaces. F H R P (first hop redundancy protocol, such as H S R P and V R R P). Two or more routers share a virtual gateway so hosts keep their default gateway if one fails. Virtual I P (V I P). The shared address hosts use as the default gateway; it moves to the surviving router. Subinterfaces. Several logical interfaces on one physical router port, one per V L A N (router on a stick). Exam tip: "Clients must keep their gateway if one router fails" equals F H R P with a virtual I P. "Route between V L A Ns with one router port" equals subinterfaces (eight oh two dot one Q trunk). Exam tip: O S P F is link-state and interior; B G P is path-vector and between organizations (autonomous systems).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A router has routes to ten dot one dot zero dot zero slash sixteen and ten dot one dot five dot zero slash twenty-four. A packet is sent to ten dot one dot five dot twenty. Which route is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: ten dot one dot five dot zero slash twenty-four, because it has the longest prefix. The most specific prefix wins.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A router learns the same prefix from O S P F (A D one hundred ten) and from a static route (A D one). Which is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The static route. Lower administrative distance wins.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Hundreds of private hosts must share one public I P address. Which technology fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Port address translation. P A T maps many private hosts to one public address using ports.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which protocol exchanges routes between autonomous systems on the internet? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: B G P. B G P is the exterior path-vector protocol.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Hosts must keep a working default gateway if the primary router fails. What should be implemented? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An F H R P such as H S R P or V R R P with a virtual I P. F H R Ps share a virtual gateway between routers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A single router interface must route traffic for three V L A Ns. What configuration is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Subinterfaces on an eight oh two dot one Q trunk. Router on a stick uses a subinterface per V L A N.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the first step of route selection? Answer: The longest (most specific) prefix. Question two. Which has the lower administrative distance, static or O S P F? Answer: Static (one versus one hundred ten). Question three. What type of protocol is O S P F? Answer: Link-state, interior.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does P A T use to separate hosts? Answer: Port numbers. Question five. What does a V I P do in an F H R P? Answer: Provides the shared default gateway address. Question six. What is a subinterface? Answer: A logical interface on a physical port, often one per V L A N.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Protocols: static (manual), O S P F (link-state), E I G R P (advanced distance-vector), B G P (path-vector, between A S es). Selection: longest prefix, then lowest A D, then lowest metric. A D: connected zero, static one, e B G P twenty, E I G R P ninety, O S P F one hundred ten, R I P one hundred twenty. nat: static and dynamic nat; P A T shares one I P using ports. Redundancy: F H R P (H S R P, V R R P) with a V I P; subinterfaces.
